newsitem.title: USA: Iowa unemployment rate falls to 2.6 pct in July.
newsitem.headline: Iowa unemployment rate falls to 2.6 pct in July.

text.p: Iowa's seasonally adjusted unemployment rate dropped to a record low 2.6 percent in July, four percentage points lower than June, the state's workforce development director reported Thursday.
"Continuing strength in Iowa's job market and the decline in plant shutdowns generated a significant decrease in the unemployment rate in July," Director Cynthia Eisenhauer said.
Recent graduates have found the job market more open than in past years as well, Eisenhauer said.
Iowa's seasonally adjusted unemployment rate in July 1996 was 3.8 percent and the state reported an increase of 17,600 jobs over one year ago.
Nonfarm employment for July showed its first monthly decline in seven months with a decrease of 2,500 jobs in the government sector and 900 in services.
Those declines were partly offset by a 700-job gain in retail trade, 400 in transportation, 200 in durable goods manufacturing and 100 in mining. Construction remained unchanged.
The national unemployment rate fell to 4.8 percent in July from 5 percent in June and 5.4 percent in July 1996.
